cases.evidence: probe-case.js --hover ".qmark": popover #m1-pop opens at rect {x:239, y:344, w:240, h:115} — below the left KPI card, over bare dashboard canvas; the second card ('Time to value') occupies x>=777, so no text/control/graphic is overlapped (screenshot confirms). BUT the same probe reports "hoverableAfterPointerTravel": false: the only hide hooks are on the 18x18 trigger (trig.addEventListener('mouseleave', hide); trig.addEventListener('blur', hide)) and the popover is positioned `top: calc(100% + 14px)` off the CARD, i.e. ~215px below the trigger, so the pointer cannot reach the popover without leaving the trigger and closing it. The pre-strip author comment concedes this in writing: "This page also has NO keyboard dismiss (no Esc handler, no close button, popover not hoverable-to-close)."
cases.reasoning: Davin's comment is correct on its own terms and I verified it: the popover covers only empty canvas, so 1.4.13's Dismissible bullet is satisfied via the non-obscuring exception, exactly as the corpus argues. The problem is that the corpus reasons about Dismissible only, while 1.4.13 also requires Hoverable — 'the pointer can be moved over the additional content without the additional content disappearing' — which has NO white-space or non-obscuring exception, and this popover measurably fails it. If that reading holds, this 'PASS control' actually fails 1.4.13 for a bullet nobody raised, and expected would flip passed->failed; alternatively the page should be repaired (mouseenter/mouseleave on #m1-pop plus a bridged position) to make it the pass control it was meant to be. Both routes are ground-truth calls for a human, so this is not FIX-OBVIOUS.

edits.oldString: Why automated tools cannot judge this page: every checker sees a valid form and a valid role="dialog" with aria-modal="true". There is no missing attribute, no empty name, no contrast defect. A naive 4.1.3 heuristic ("a message appeared after submit but no role=status / aria-live exists") would FALSELY flag this dialog. Deciding that the error here is exempt requires a human to recognize that the dialog took focus — a change of context that is already announced — so the status-message definition is not met and the SC does not apply. That is a semantic + behavioral call, not a DOM pattern.
